one_liner: C++17 SIMD node-graph noise library (Perlin, Simplex, Value, Cellular) that generates arrays 4-8x faster than scalar FastNoise Lite.
what_it_does: Generates coherent noise (Perlin, Simplex, SuperSimplex/OpenSimplex2S, Value, Cellular), fractals (FBm, Ridged), domain warps, blends and modifiers in 2D, 3D and 4D. You build a tree of nodes in code (FastNoise::New<FastNoise::Simplex>(), SetSource) or load an encoded string exported from the bundled Node Editor, then fill a caller-allocated float array with GenUniformGrid2D/3D/4D, GenPositionArray, or GenTileable2D. It is not a drop-in for per-point APIs like FastNoise Lite's GetNoise(x, y); a per-point GenSingle2D/3D/4D exists but the header itself labels it 'VERY SLOW'.
how_it_is_fast: Each node is compiled once per SIMD feature set (scalar, SSE2, SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX-512, NEON, WASM SIMD) through the author's FastSIMD abstraction and dispatched at runtime to the best one the CPU supports. The whole node tree is evaluated per SIMD batch, so intermediate values of combined noises stay in registers instead of being written to separate arrays and recombined in scalar passes (the README's 'Why Nodes?' argument). The default build also enables fast-math (-ffast-math or /fp:fast) on the SIMD kernels unless FASTNOISE2_STRICT_FP is set.
when_to_use: Bulk generation of noise fields: terrain heightmaps, voxel chunks (e.g. 64^3 grids), 3D density fields, procedural textures, where you fill whole arrays per call.
Layered noise (fractal FBm, domain warp, blends of several noise types) where fusing the whole graph in SIMD avoids extra memory passes.
x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512, or ARM with NEON, when a scalar library such as FastNoise Lite, libnoise or stb_perlin is a bottleneck in world or texture generation.
Teams that want artists or designers to tune noise in a visual Node Editor and ship the encoded string, with the same tree callable from C++, C#, Rust, Java or Unreal bindings.
Multi-threaded chunk generation: generation methods are const and documented as thread-safe on a shared node tree.
when_not_to_use: Per-point sampling scattered through game logic (one value at a time): GenSingle* underuses SIMD lanes; FastNoise Lite's header-only scalar API is simpler there.

You need bit-identical output across CPUs or platforms without extra work: the default build uses fast-math and FMA on some feature sets, open issue #147 asks exactly this, and a 2026-10-10 fix (#189) removed AVX2 versus SSE2 differences of up to 0.133 in 4D Simplex domain warp; build with FASTNOISE2_STRICT_FP for exact matching.

Projects that cannot fetch dependencies at configure time or want a single header: FastNoise2 is a compiled CMake library that pulls FastSIMD through CPM, and the standalone build also builds the Node Editor by default.
Building with plain MSVC on Windows: the README says MSVC has SIMD compiler bugs that cause incorrect generation and recommends clang-cl.
You rely on the 2020 benchmark numbers for current code: v1.0.0 (January 2026) changed the generation API and several kernels, and no comparison table has been published for it.

integration.dependencies: FastSIMD (downloaded by CPM at configure time, pinned to commit 16450dae); the optional Node Editor pulls further GUI dependencies
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.10; clang-cl recommended over MSVC on Windows; GCC and Clang supported (exact minimum compiler versions not documented)
integration.platforms: x86 32/64-bit (scalar, SSE2, SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX-512 selected at runtime), ARM (NEON on armv7a and aarch64), WASM SIMD; Windows, Linux, macOS x86/ARM, Android, iOS, Emscripten
integration.thread_safety: Generation methods are const and documented as fully thread-safe; one node tree can be shared across threads (Generator.h). Setting node parameters while other threads generate is not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same noise families as FastNoise Lite, but a different interface (node objects plus bulk array generation instead of GetNoise(x, y[, z])); frequency is now expressed through step size and per-node feature size, so outputs are not identical to FastNoise Lite

gotchas: Harness flaw (asymmetric build flags): at the pinned 2020 commit e191bc2 FastNoise2's own CMake compiled its library with /GS- /fp:fast (the if(MSVC) branch also fires for clang-cl) and its AVX2 file with -mavx2 -mfma, while the FastNoise Lite, FastNoise legacy, libnoise and stb_perlin benchmark DLLs got no extra flags (strict FP, SSE2 baseline). The README's 'clang-cl 10.0.0 -m64 /O2' line does not describe this, and the harness's only release configuration in CMakeSettings.json is RelWithDebInfo (/O2 /Ob1).

The comparison is not like-for-like in API or noise type: FastNoise2 fills a 512x512 or 64^3 float array via GenUniformGrid (frequency 0.02), while each scalar library is called once per point through GetNoise inside benchmark::DoNotOptimize (FastNoise Lite at its default frequency). The FastNoise Lite adapter has no Simplex case, so both its 2D 'Simplex' and 3D '*OpenSimplex' numbers are OpenSimplex2 runs; against the like-for-like FastNoise legacy Simplex the 3D ratio is 6.0x (derived from page data). The author's own SIMD predecessor FastNoiseSIMD is built and run by the harness but left out of the README table.

The README table cannot be reproduced against current code: the harness calls GenUniformGrid2D(out, int xStart, int yStart, xSize, ySize, float frequency, seed) and FastSIMD::Level_AVX2, while v1.0.0 changed GenUniformGrid to (out, float xOffset, ..., int xCount, ..., float xStepSize, ..., seed) and moved to FastSIMD FeatureSet; Google Benchmark runs once per case (Repetitions commented out) and no raw output is committed.

Recent correctness fixes change output: #191 (2026-10-09) fixed CellularDistance Euclidean returning sqrt(F2) when both distance indices are equal and NaN at distance 0 with zero jitter; #190 applies the domain-warp seed offset once; #189 fixed 4D Simplex domain warp differing between feature sets. The default cellular configuration used in the benchmark is not affected by #191.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FastNoise2 over SIMDNoise (rust-simd-noise) when you work in C++ and want a node graph with fused fractal, warp and blend operations plus AVX-512, NEON and WASM paths; pick it over writing noise kernels yourself with ISPC, EVE or the Vector Class Library when standard Perlin, Simplex, Value or Cellular noise is all you need.
verified_claims_summary: On an Intel 7820X at 4.9 GHz under Windows 10 with clang-cl 10, the author's NoiseBenchmarking harness measured a September 2020 FastNoise2 snapshot (forced to AVX2, bulk GenUniformGrid) at 262-776 million points per second for 2D and 3D Value, Perlin and Simplex and 52-194 for Cellular, about 4.2x to 7.7x the per-point scalar FastNoise Lite (derived from page data). The FastNoise2 side was built with fast-math and FMA and the scalar side without, and the numbers predate the v1.0.0 API and kernel changes.
status_note: Actively maintained (v1.1.1 in February 2026, correctness fixes through 2026-10-10), MIT-licensed, with C#, Rust, Java and Unreal bindings; the published library comparison has not been rerun since 2020.
